Chocolate Plus Firmware analysis

Home Custom Firmware Build from source
What we found out about the firmware of the M-VAVE Chocolate Plus (FootCtrlPlus).

These notes come from analysing the original firmware 012 so that the custom firmware could be built and the pedal configured with our own tools. The page describes formats, algorithms and addresses. It contains no M-VAVE or JieLi code (see what is not published). All numbers refer to the original firmware 012 unless noted.

Device and chip

ProductM-VAVE Chocolate Plus, Bluetooth name and firmware name FootCtrlPlus, board marking PD41 V04
ChipJieLi AC636N (BR25 family), CPU core pi32v2, internal flash, Bluetooth LE + Classic
Original firmwareFootCtrlPlus_012 (version 012). Distributed as FootCtrlPlus_012.fwsc (583476 bytes)
Update toolsSincoOTA (Android) and the CubeSuite app, both over Bluetooth LE
Development toolsJieLi toolchain 2.5.3 (clang for pi32v2) and the public JieLi AC63 SDK (github.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AC63_BT_SDK), which matches the firmware's structure
Display3-digit 7-segment display, driven through a 74HC164 shift register
Mode switchU / O / H: U = USB, O = off, H = host (USB and Bluetooth). U is also used to force USB download mode.

.fwsc file (Sinco wrapper)

A .fwsc file is a JieLi .ufw file with 20 extra bytes woven in: after every 47 bytes of the .ufw, one metadata byte is inserted, 20 times. The rest of the file follows unchanged. Removing bytes 47, 95, 143, … (every 48th byte, 20 times) gives the original .ufw.

  • The 20 metadata bytes hold the name <name>_<version><suffix>, padded with @.
  • Each name character is stored as char + i + 1 (i = position, 0-based), padding is stored as is. Example 012: stored GqrxHzytYv… → FootCtrlPlus_012.
  • SincoOTA decodes the name with the length of the file name, so the file must keep its name (e.g. FootCtrlPlus_141-dtnprt.fwsc). A renamed file is rejected or misread.
  • The version digits in the name are what the apps show as firmware version; they must be digits only.

.ufw container (JieLi)

All numbers little-endian. The 64-byte header and every table entry are scrambled (see scrambling); the members themselves are stored at their offsets.

Header (0x40 bytes, scrambled)

0x00u16header CRC over header bytes 0x02..0x3f (descrambled)0x0002
0x02u16table CRC over the table as stored (scrambled)0x9ac1
0x04u32total file size583456
0x08u16number of members8
0x10char[]chip nameAC636N

Member table (count × 0x50 bytes from offset 0x40, each entry scrambled on its own)

OffsetTypeMeaning
0x00u8flag/type byte (differs per member, meaning not needed)
0x02u16member index
0x04u16member CRC (CRC-16 over the stored member bytes; verified for the code members)
0x08u32offset in the file
0x0cu32size
0x10u32size rounded up (alignment)

A patch has to change flash.bin and flash2.bin identically; the other members stay untouched.

flash.bin and the app area

  • flash.bin starts with a 0x1000-byte boot header in plain form (it contains the chip ID string AC636N_TRANS at 0x10).
  • From offset 0x1000 follows the app area, encrypted (see key). Decrypted, app-area offset 0 is CPU address 0x01e00000 (code runs from flash at this address).

App area layout (decrypted)

OffsetContent
0x00area header: u16 header CRC over 0x02..0x1f, u16 data CRC over 0x20..area_len, u32 area length at 0x08 (012: 0x26410), name app_area_head
0x20entry for app.bin: u16 header CRC over 0x22..0x3f, u16 code CRC, u32 code address 0x24 (012: 0x120), u32 code length 0x28 (012: 0x25f90), name app.bin
0x120application code; entry point 0x01e00120

Scrambling, encryption and key

Both layers use the same JieLi LFSR (linear feedback shift register, 32-bit state); the keystream byte is the low byte of the state after each step. Both are plain XOR, so the same function encrypts and decrypts. A reference implementation is lfsr_next() in firmware/fwsctool.py of the repository; the browser patcher contains the same in JavaScript.

Header and table scrambling

  • Applied to the 0x40-byte .ufw header and to each 0x50-byte table entry separately.
  • Byte 0 is inverted (~b); bytes 1… are XORed with the keystream, state seeded with 0xffff.

Member encryption (the key)

  • Works in 32-byte blocks. For each block the state is seeded with key XOR (pos >> 2); byte 0 of the block is XORed with the seed's low byte, the following bytes with the keystream; then pos advances by 32.
  • pos is a start value per member (address-like), not the offset in the file.
DataKeyStart pos
App area = flash.bin from 0x1000 (same for flash2.bin)0x180f0x20000
isd_config.ini0x180f0x7a00

Check: with the right parameters the app-area CRC chain verifies and the text app.bin appears at 0x30. Our first attempt with other parameters (0x9d0f / 0x1400) decrypted only about 40 % of the blocks correctly.

Checksums

All checksums are CRC-16/XMODEM (polynomial 0x1021, start value 0, no final XOR). After changing code, they must be rebuilt in this order:

  1. app.bin code CRC (entry 0x22), then the entry's header CRC (0x20)
  2. app area data CRC (0x02), then the area header CRC (0x00)
  3. re-encrypt the app area, member CRC in the .ufw table entry (re-scramble the entry)
  4. table CRC and header CRC in the .ufw header (re-scramble the header)
  5. wrap as .fwsc with the name of the new file

Self-test used by build.py: rebuilding the chain on the unchanged original must reproduce it byte for byte.

Free space for patches

The flash is almost full. Usable: the unreferenced functions at 0x1e00406 (104 bytes) and 0x1e11b06 (68 bytes), the 0xff padding at 0x1e19308 (32 bytes) and 0x1e26088 (40 bytes).

Footswitch handling

Each switch has a small state machine in the 5 ms poll:

  1. idle → pressed for D consecutive ticks → pending (counter = 0)
  2. pending → still pressed when the counter reaches F → pressed, press event sent
  3. pending → released before F → back to idle, no event

The pending window exists to detect two switches pressed together (A+B, C+D combos). Original values: D = 4, F = 15 ticks.

  • Press latency (4 + 15) × 5 ms ≈ 95 ms.
  • Any tap shorter than that was silently lost (case 3).

Custom firmware: D = 3, F = 6 (≈ 45 ms, combo window 30 ms), and a released switch in the pending state goes to the press path, so short taps send press + release.

Bank number bug (advanced custom mode)

The displayed bank was counted up/down from its own value instead of the saved bank index. After power-on it started at 0, and bank-down showed an invalid bank (255). The selected presets were always correct, only the number was wrong.

Display, battery, status LED

  • Segments (one byte per digit): a = bit 6, b = bit 3, c = bit 2, d = bit 0, e = bit 1, f = bit 7, g = bit 4, dot = bit 5.
  • The 5 ms poll shifts the segment byte into the 74HC164 (data GPIO 0x16, clock GPIO 0x15) and selects one of the 3 digits per tick.
  • The font has no K, M, V, W, X, Z (blank). U can stand in for V, n for M.
  • Status LED on PA0. Port A registers at 0x1e5000: OUT +0, IN +4, DIR +8 (1 = input), pull-up +0x10, pull-down +0x14. The pull-up alone is too weak to light the LED; dimming works by driving it in one of the three digit slots (1/3 duty, ~67 Hz).
  • Holding B+C for about 2 s switches Bluetooth off and on (not the LED); the LED is dark while Bluetooth is off.

cmdMeaningPayload

Memory types: NOR = 0, NAND = 1, SD = 2, EFF = 3, DEV = 4 (settings), USR = 5, RAM = 6.

Settings block (DEV, address 0, 23646 bytes)

OffsetSizeField
01mode (0…12)
11TRS MIDI on/off
21MIDI channel (0…16)
310user values [5][2]
1380tap MIDI codes [16]
9313344advanced custom: 8 banks × 4 switches, 417 bytes each
1343772custom keys [6][4][3]
1350910128mixed keys [6][4], 422 bytes each

MIDI code = 5 bytes: enabled, channel, type, data1, data2. Advanced-custom entry (417 bytes) = mode + 16 MIDI codes (A) + 16 MIDI codes (B) + SysEx A (128) + SysEx B (128). The Web Config uses exactly this protocol.

Firmware update (OTA)

The update uses JieLi's RCSP protocol on service ae00, as documented in the public JieLi SDK.

FE DC BA | flags | opcode | length (u16, big-endian) | [status] | sequence | parameters | EF
flags: bit 7 = command, bit 6 = reply wanted
OpcodeMeaning
03target info (capabilities, single/dual bank, MTU)
E1where the firmware info is in the file (offset, length)
E2can the device update with this file? (0 = yes)
E3enter update mode
E5device requests a block (offset u32, length u16); the host answers with those file bytes
E6update result
E7reboot
E8total size
0Bchange communication way (reconnect)

Two phases (the pedal is single-bank with an update loader)

  1. E1 → E2 → the device pulls the loader (ota.bin) with E8/E5 → E6 → 0B: the pedal restarts into its update loader.
  2. Reconnect, the device now reports "mandatory upgrade" → E1 → E2 → E3 → E8/E5 for the whole file → E6 = 0 → E7 reboot.

If phase 2 is interrupted, the pedal stays in its loader and can be flashed again (SincoOTA → Mandatory upgrade). The loader itself is never overwritten, so the original firmware can always be restored this way.

Connection authentication

Before any command, app and pedal authenticate each other: each side sends a 16-byte random challenge, the other answers with the Bluetooth legacy E1 function (SAFER+) computed with a fixed key from JieLi's library, then both confirm with pass. The key is not published here (see below).

USB download and recovery

  • Normal recovery: flash the original FootCtrlPlus_012.fwsc with SincoOTA. Works as long as the pedal starts Bluetooth.
  • Last resort: the chip's ROM bootloader accepts a full flash download over USB with JieLi's download tool, independent of the app.
  • The decrypted isd_config.ini of 012 describes the flash setup: chip AC636N, entry 0x1E00120, product ID AC636N_TRANS, download over USB, reset/download pin PB01, UART PB05, 39 settings in total.
  • The chip also has a JTAG debug interface on the board.

Pitfalls we hit

  • Wrong decryption parameters give plausible-looking but partly garbled code. Always verify with the CRC chain.
  • "Unused" code is not always unused: a function without direct calls (0x1e04a84) is reached through a pointer when a Bluetooth pairing is stored. Reusing it as free space crashed the pedal on pairing.
  • Both copies: flash.bin and flash2.bin must carry the same patch.
  • Name matters: the .fwsc must keep its file name, and the Bluetooth name must stay FootCtrlPlus.
  • LED via pull-up is too dark; it has to be driven as output.
  • Pairing: for updates the pedal must not be paired with the phone.

What is not published

This page only contains facts about formats, interfaces and addresses, found while making the pedal work with our own software. On purpose it does not contain:

  • M-VAVE's or JieLi's firmware, tools or apps, in whole or in part (no downloads, no hex dumps of their code)
  • disassembly listings or decompiled source code of the firmware or the apps
  • vendor manuals, documents or screenshots
  • the authentication key of the update protocol
  • addresses of non-public vendor servers

The original firmware is available from M-VAVE: Chocolate Plus product page. Not affiliated with M-VAVE, Sinco or JieLi. All product names belong to their owners.
